==English==
{{wp}}

===Etymology===
From {{inh|en|enm|slaw}}, {{m|enm|slow}}, from {{inh|en|ang|slāw|t=lazy; inert, slow}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*slaiw}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*slaiwaz|t=blunt; dull; exhausted, faint, sluggish, weak, weary; listless, torpid; dim-witted, slow; lazy, slack}}, possibly from {{der|en|ine-pro|*(s)leyH-|*sleyH-u-|bad}}.
{{col-top|2|cog}}
Cognate with {{cog|nl|slee}}, {{m|nl|sleeuw|t=cramped, stiff; blunt; sour}}, {{cog|da|sløv|t=blunt; dull; apathetic, lethargic, listless, sluggish, torpid; drowsy}}, {{cog|is|sljór|t=dim-witted; blunt; jaded}}, {{cog|nn|sljo}}, {{m|nn|slø}}, {{m|nn|sløv|t=blunt; weak; lazy}}, {{cog|sv|slö|t=dull; lazy, lethargic, slow, sluggish}}.
{{col-bottom}}

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/sləʊ/|a=UK}}
** {{audio|en|En-uk-slow.ogg|a=UK}}
** {{IPA|en|/slaː/|a=Northumbria}}
* {{IPA|en|/sloʊ/|a=US}}
** {{audio|en|en-us-slow.ogg|a=US}}
* {{rhymes|en|əʊ|s=1}}
* {{homophones|en|sloe}}

===Adjective===
{{en-adj|er}}

# Taking a long [[time]] to move or go a short [[distance]], or to perform an action; not [[quick]] in [[motion]]; [[proceed]]ing at a [[low]] speed.
#: {{ux|en|a '''slow''' train;  a '''slow''' computer}}
#: {{ux|en|Why were you so '''slow''' to answer my question?}}
#: {{ux|en|Turkey should always be cooked in a [[slow oven|'''slow''' oven]].}}
#* {{RQ:Economist|date=2013-07-20|volume=408|issue=8845
|title=[http://www.economist.com/news/http://www.economist.com/news/business/21582001-army-new-online-courses-scaring-wits-out-traditional-universities-can-they The attack of the MOOCs]
|passage=Dotcom mania was '''slow''' in coming to higher education, but now it has the venerable industry firmly in its grip. Since the launch early last year of Udacity and Coursera, two Silicon Valley start-ups offering free education through MOOCs, massive open online courses, the ivory towers of academia have been shaken to their foundations.}}
# Not happening in a short time; [[spread]] over a comparatively long time.
#* {{RQ:Milton Paradise Lost|lines=692–695|sig=[Mm3]|verso=1|page=279|text=Theſe changes in the Heav’ns, though '''ſlow''', produc’d / Like change on Sea and Land, ſideral blaſt, / Vapour, and Miſt, and Exhalation hot, / Corrupt and Peſtilent: {{...}}}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|year=2013|month=May–June|author=[http://www.americanscientist.org/authors/detail/charles-t-ambrose Charles T. Ambrose]
|title=[http://www.americanscientist.org/issues/feature/2013/3/alzheimerrsquos-disease-the-great-morbidity-of-the-21st-century Alzheimer’s Disease]
|volume=101|issue=3|page=200|magazine=w:American Scientist
|passage=Similar studies of rats have employed four different intracranial resorbable, '''slow''' sustained release systems—surgical foam, a thermal gel depot, a microcapsule or biodegradable polymer beads.}}
# {{lb|en|informal|somewhat|derogatory}} Of [[reduce]]d [[intellectual]] [[capacity]]; not quick to [[comprehend]].
#* {{quote-journal|en|year=1960|work=Dissertation Abstracts|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=hyAhAQAAMAAJ|volume=20|page=4007|passage=Experienced classroom teachers are well acquainted with the attention-seeker, the shy girl, the aggressive boy, the poor concentrator, the '''slow''' student,{{nb...}}}}
# Not [[hasty]]; not tending to [[hurry]]; acting with [[deliberation]] or caution.
#* {{RQ:KJV|Proverbs|xiv|29|passage=He that is '''slow''' to wrath is of great understanding.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1999|author=Brian Paul Kaufman; K. Winston Caine|title=Prayer, Faith, and Healing: Cure Your Body, Heal Your Mind and Restore Your Soul|passage=And even after the emotional cast comes off, we need to be '''slow''' about getting deeply involved in a relationship again.}}
# {{lb|en|of a [[clock]] or the like}} [[behind|Behind]] in time; indicating a time [[early|earlier]] than the [[true]] time.
#: {{ux|en|That clock is '''slow'''.}}
# Lacking [[spirit]]; [[deficient]] in [[liveliness]] or [[briskness]].
# {{lb|en|of a period of time}} Not [[busy]]; lacking [[activity]].
#: {{ux|en|It was a '''slow''' news day, so the editor asked us to make our articles wordier.}}
#: {{ux|en|I'm just sitting here with a desk of cards, enjoying a '''slow''' afternoon.}}

====Synonyms====
* {{sense|taking a long time to move a short distance}} {{l|en|deliberate}}; {{l|en|moderate}}; see also [[Thesaurus:slow]]

* {{sense|of reduced intellectual capacity}} {{l|en|dull-witted}}; see also [[Thesaurus:stupid]]
* {{sense|acting with deliberation}} {{l|en|careful}}, {{l|en|deliberate}}, {{l|en|prudent}}; see also [[Thesaurus:cautious]]

* {{sense|lacking spirit}} {{l|en|boring}}, {{l|en|dilatory}}, {{l|en|dull}}, {{l|en|inactive}}, {{l|en|tardy}}, {{l|en|slothful}}, {{l|en|sluggish}}; see also [[Thesaurus:inactive]] or [[Thesaurus:boring]]
* {{sense|not busy}} {{l|en|quiet}}, {{l|en|unbusy}}

====Antonyms====

* {{antsense|of reduced intellectual capacity}} {{l|en|keen}}, {{l|en|quick}}, {{l|en|quick-witted}}; see also [[Thesaurus:intelligent]]
* {{antsense|acting with deliberation}} {{l|en|hasty}}, {{l|en|precipitate}}, {{l|en|prompt}}; see also [[Thesaurus:prompt]]
* {{antsense|behind in time}} {{l|en|accurate}}, {{l|en|fast}}
* {{antsense|lacking spirit}} {{l|en|brisk}}, {{l|en|lively}}; see also [[Thesaurus:active]]
* {{antsense|not busy}} {{l|en|hectic}}

===Verb===
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|transitive}} To make (something) [[run]], [[move]], etc. less [[quickly]]; to [[reduce]] the [[speed]] of.
#: {{ux|en|'''slow''' the process}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To keep from going quickly; to [[hinder]] the [[progress]] of.
#: {{ux|en|'''slow''' the traffic}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To become slow; to [[slacken]] in [[speed]]; to [[decelerate]].
#* {{RQ:NYT|date=26 December 2012|author=[[w:John Branch (journalist)|John Branch]]|title=Snow Fall: The Avalanche at Tunnel Creek|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20131114133825/http://www.nytimes.com/projects/2012/snow-fall/?smid=fb-nytimes&WT.z_sma=SP_SNT_20130415#/?part=tunnel-creek|passage=After about a minute, the creek bed vomited the debris into a gently sloped meadow. Saugstad felt the snow '''slow''' and tried to keep her hands in front of her.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=2022 January 12|author=Benedict le Vay|title=The heroes of Soham...|journal=RAIL|issue=948|page=42|text=As he passed though the station, he '''slowed''' to yell to the signalman, Frank 'Sailor' Bridges: "Sailor - have you anything between here and Fordham? Where's the mail?" Gimbert knew the mail train was due, and he didn't want to endanger another train with his burning bomb wagon.}}

* {{sense|become slow}} {{l|en|decelerate}}, {{l|en|slacken}}
